key_insight: Ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces by removing excess tin, improving electron extraction and suppressing interfacial nonradiative recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling surface stoichiometry and passivant chemistry offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine with protonated ethylenediammonium iodide surface treatments.
Use atomistic simulations to examine vacancy-assisted iodide migration and deprotonation.
Link surface reconstruction to n-type character, electron extraction into C60, and device performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency in methylammonium-free solar cells and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: Long-term operational stability and manufacturing-scale reproducibility are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
